headline: Benchmarks and new callers refine variant, indel, and fusion detection
label: Genomic Variant Detection Methods
summary: Pangenome graph references and GIAB-benchmarked platforms are now being applied to somatic, complex indel, and fusion variant calling.
synthesis: The dominant thread is improving how variants are detected and prioritized when platform, reference, and sequence-homology factors bias calls. A GIAB-referenced benchmark of DNBSEQ-T7 trio WGS compares three library prep workflows, while a simulation study of six callers finds FreeBayes best represents complex indels as single records. Pansoma applies machine learning to pangenome graph tensors from short and long reads to reduce linear-reference bias in somatic calling. Fuscan filters homologous regions to reduce false-positive fusions in targeted cancer panels, reporting AUC 0.992. A benchmark of hg38, CHM13, pangenome, and personal phased assemblies shows reference choice affects functional genomics analyses, and GDIv2 refines exome variant selection by correcting the Gene Damage Index for coding length and normalizing CADD per gene. A pan-cancer analysis of 2,157 WGS tumors links SSA and Alt-EJ deletion scars to SINE content and transcription start sites beyond HR deficiency. What is new is graph-based and simulation-driven evaluation applied directly to variant calling.
